title: The Monsoon of the Sepik Basin
premise: Casper Iversen, a disgraced railroad engineer drifting through Papua New Guinea's Sepik Basin with a map of closed lines and a talent for not being found, is hired to escort a supply run to a hydrological expedition upriver. When the expedition's radio goes silent, Casper discovers the team has uncovered evidence that a colonial-era mining consortium buried a massacre and diverted a river to hide it — and that one of its descendants now funds the region's new development push. To bring the survivors home before glacier calving opens the route for only a few weeks, Casper must navigate crocodile waters, hostile middlemen, and his own growing love for expedition cartographer Mara Ellingsen, who insists the truth go public while Casper knows publication will get them all killed. In the end, Casper chooses a third path: he delivers the survivors safely, then anonymously mails the evidence to a tribunal and the dead men's families, sacrificing his invisibility forever — and staying, for the first time in his life, in one place.
about_author: Silas Thornbury is the pen name of a former survey engineer who spent eleven years mapping river routes across Southeast Asia and Melanesia before turning to fiction. He writes from a houseboat on an unnamed tributary, where he claims the best plots arrive with the wet season.

chapters.title: The Man Who Owns No Address
chapters.summary: Casper Iversen's POV. In Wewak, Casper takes odd survey jobs under borrowed names, haunted by a collapsed trestle he was blamed for years ago. A fixer named Okuk offers him a lucrative escort contract upriver. Beat: restless isolation cracked open by temptation.

chapters.title: A Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Casper studies the contract: supplies for a hydrological team at a decommissioned gauge station near the headwaters. The map shows rail spurs abandoned since the war — lines someone paid to erase. Beat: curiosity overriding caution.

chapters.title: The Cartographer Who Argues With Rivers
chapters.summary: Mara Ellingsen's POV. At the staging camp, Mara re-draws channel charts the official maps get wrong, clashing with expedition lead Dr. Hargreave over safety margins. She notices Casper reading water like a local. Beat: wary mutual recognition.

chapters.title: Manifest of Small Lies
chapters.summary: Casper inventories the cargo and finds crates mislabeled as instruments — drilling gear, sample vaults, and a satellite phone no one admits to owning. Beat: first concrete sign the expedition is hunting something, not measuring it.

chapters.title: Departure at First Light
chapters.summary: The convoy of boats pushes into the Sepik's braided channels. Casper navigates; Hargreave radiates confidence; young geologist Tomas befriends Casper over engine repairs. Beat: fragile camaraderie on moving water.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't on Any Chart
chapters.summary: A river community hosts them overnight. An elder recognizes the gauge station's name and goes quiet, saying only that the river was 'moved by men who counted bodies as ballast.' Beat: history surfacing through silence.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: Casper's POV. The expedition's scheduled check-in with Wewak fails; the backup frequency returns static. Hargreave insists it's equipment. Casper checks the antenna — cut clean. Beat: dread arriving before danger.

chapters.title: What the Water Gives Back
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Sampling reveals sediment layers impossible for natural flow — the river was rerouted decades ago above the station. Mara starts her own quiet map of anomalies. Beat: the scientist's thrill curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Crocodile Bank
chapters.summary: A night crossing goes wrong; a boat swamps and Tomas nearly drowns in croc water. Casper pulls him out, earning the crew's trust but revealing skills beyond 'escort.' Beat: competence exposed, bonds forged.

chapters.title: The Gauge Station
chapters.summary: They reach the station: ransacked, radios smashed, and a fresh grave marked with a survey stake. One expedition member, Dr. Ferro, is missing. Beat: the mission changes from delivery to rescue.

chapters.title: Ferro's Last Notebook
chapters.summary: Hidden in a fuel drum, Ferro's notes describe a sealed adit behind the gauge station — a wartime mine tunnel containing ledgers, photographs, and bones. The last entry names a buyer coming to collect them. Beat: the past has a pulse.

chapters.title: Hargreave's Real Employer
chapters.summary: Casper confronts Hargreave, who confesses the dig was funded by the Kessler Development Group — heir to the colonial consortium — ostensibly for 'heritage recovery.' Hargreave believes he can negotiate. Beat: duty and greed wearing each other's clothes.

chapters.title: Downstream Eyes
chapters.summary: Casper spots a patrol boat running dark upriver — hired security, too well-equipped for prospectors. He scatters decoy camps and kills their lights. Beat: the hunter becomes the hunted.

chapters.title: Mara's Choice
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. She photographs the ledgers' location data and argues the evidence must reach a tribunal. Casper argues it will get everyone killed first. Their argument ends closer than either intended. Beat: love kindling inside conflict.

chapters.title: The Adit
chapters.summary: Casper, Mara, and Tomas enter the mine tunnel: rusted rails (matching Casper's closed-line map), a collapse hiding a chamber of company ledgers, execution photos, and remains. Beat: horror made bureaucratic.

chapters.title: Bones and Ballast
chapters.summary: Tomas identifies his own grandfather among the laborers listed as 'expended.' He breaks down; Casper, who knows about inherited guilt, sits with him through the night. Beat: grief as common ground.

chapters.title: The Buyer Arrives
chapters.summary: Kessler Group representative Anselm Roos lands by floatplane with the security detail, offering Hargreave a fortune to hand over the ledgers and sign a confidentiality clause. Hargreave wavers visibly. Beat: corruption making a polite offer.

chapters.title: Negotiation at Gunpoint
chapters.summary: Roos's patience expires; the crew is detained at the station. Casper, presumed harmless, is left unbound — a mistake he begins quietly exploiting. Beat: humiliation sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Radio Trick
chapters.summary: Casper repairs a hidden backup transmitter and broadcasts a false distress call downstream, pulling half of Roos's men toward a phantom wreck. Beat: the invisible man becomes the puppeteer.

chapters.title: Escape Through the Sudd
chapters.summary: Mara pilots the remaining boat through a maze of floating vegetation she alone has charted. They lose the supplies but keep the ledgers, the photos, and Ferro — found alive, feverish, hiding upstream. Beat: triumph with a cost.

chapters.title: Fever Dreams
chapters.summary: Mara's POV. Nursing Ferro, Mara learns Roos's deadline: the evidence must be destroyed before the tribunal session in Port Moresby. She and Casper plan openly now — together. Beat: partnership sealed by shared risk.

chapters.title: Roos Closes the River
chapters.summary: Roos buys the district's river police with a phone call; checkpoints bloom at every junction. The legal route home is gone. Beat: power showing how cheaply it purchases law.

chapters.title: The Old Survey Road
chapters.summary: Casper proposes the impossible: portage overland along a closed rail spur from his map to a disused airfield. Hargreave objects — until Roos's men burn the station behind them. Beat: the coward's arithmetic finally fails.

chapters.title: Portage
chapters.summary: The grueling carry over jungle ridges; leeches, injuries, and Hargreave's breakdown when he admits he knew about the massacre's cover-up from the start. Beat: confession as penance, leadership transferred to Casper.

chapters.title: Okuk's Price
chapters.summary: At a trading post, fixer Okuk offers to smuggle them to the airfield — for the ledgers themselves, to sell back to Kessler. Casper must decide whether his oldest ally is a lifeline or a trap. Beat: betrayal wearing a friendly face.

chapters.title: Double-Cross at the Post
chapters.summary: Casper pre-empts Okuk, feeding him a fake ledger case while the real evidence travels with Mara. Okuk's buyers raid the wrong cache; gunfire; they slip away during the chaos. Beat: cunning over strength.

chapters.title: The Airfield in the Grass
chapters.summary: They reach the strip — runway swallowed by kunai grass, one derelict plane. Casper, who once certified aircraft ferries, begins a three-day repair with tools scavenged from the rail depot. Beat: hope built by hand.

chapters.title: Roos Lands
chapters.summary: Roos's floatplane arrives with mercenaries. In the standoff, Hargreave walks out offering himself and the ledgers in exchange for the crew's lives — redemption priced honestly. Roos accepts the man, not the mercy. Beat: sacrifice refused.

chapters.title: Takeoff Into the Storm
chapters.summary: Casper gets the plane airborne through a squall line as mercenaries shoot out the tail cone. They limp to a missionary strip, alive but stranded far from anywhere. Beat: survival as a narrow, screaming thing.

chapters.title: The Missionary's Radio
chapters.summary: From the mission, Casper raises an old contact — a tribunal investigator he once testified for, the same case that ruined him. She warns: evidence needs a chain of custody, or Kessler buries it again. Beat: the law offers a narrow door.

chapters.title: What Casper Knows About Falling
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, flashback woven in: the trestle collapse, the report he signed under pressure, the career that ended so a company could survive. He understands exactly how Kessler will bury this — because he helped bury something once. Beat: the villain was never a stranger.

chapters.title: Glacier Season
chapters.summary: Word comes: calving season will open the high pass route in nine days — the only window to move the evidence and witnesses out together. Roos knows it too. Beat: the clock becomes a character.

chapters.title: The Witness Train
chapters.summary: Casper organizes villagers descended from the massacre laborers to move as witnesses, using the old rail bed — his closed lines — as a covert corridor. The community that once stayed silent chooses to walk. Beat: justice as collective act.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Trestle
chapters.summary: Roos's mercenaries strike at a ruined viaduct. Tomas holds the crossing under fire and is gravely wounded; Mara drags him clear. Casper collapses a span behind them, cutting pursuit. Beat: courage measured in blood.

chapters.title: Roos Unmasked
chapters.summary: Cornered, Roos offers Casper everything — money, reinstatement, a clean name — if the ledgers burn. Casper answers with the one thing Roos can't buy: testimony of his own complicity, offered freely. Beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Pass Opens
chapters.summary: The calving season cracks the high route open; the convoy crosses as ice groans overhead, carrying witnesses, ledgers, and the dying Hargreave's sworn statement. Beat: nature granting the brief window promised from page one.

chapters.title: Port Moresby, Day One
chapters.summary: The tribunal convenes. Mara presents the physical evidence; the witnesses testify; Kessler's lawyers attack the chain of custody — until Casper stands and enters his own authenticated survey records linking the tunnels to the company. Beat: the invisible man makes himself permanent record.

chapters.title: Verdicts
chapters.summary: Roos is indicted; Kessler's projects freeze; Hargreave dies awaiting sentencing, his statement posthumously vindicating the dead. Okuk, surprisingly, testifies about the buyers. Beat: justice arriving imperfect but real.

chapters.title: The Map of Open Lines
chapters.summary: Months later, Casper oversees rebuilding the spur as a memorial railway to the laborers, his name on the drawings for the first time. Mara charts the restored river route beside him. Beat: love choosing to stay.

chapters.title: Monsoon
chapters.summary: Casper's POV, final. The wet season arrives; the river runs full over ground that remembers. Casper, who kept moving because stopping cost more, watches the rain from a porch he owns and finds the cost worth paying. Beat: stillness earned.
